item.title: Who gets to shape AI? UN debate centres on power, trust and inclusion
item.description: Artificial Intelligence or AI – and the technology behind it – is moving fast. The question being asked across the world is who gets a seat at the table deciding how it's used and who gets to benefit.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Could a new global panel defuse inequality’s ‘ticking time bomb’?
item.description: What if the world tackled inequality with the same kind of scientific firepower it has brought to the climate crisis?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Clean your plate – to reduce food loss and waste
item.description: Food waste is helping to fuel global warming, one half-eaten sandwich at a time.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Africa needs its own AI solutions, not borrowed ones, says expert
item.description: Africa should focus its use of technology on solving its own real challenges rather than copying the systems and priorities of other parts of the world.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Right to development: A blueprint for unmet promises
item.description: Ahead of the 40th anniversary of the groundbreaking Declaration on the Right to Development this December, world leaders gathered at a High-Level Week meeting on Wednesday to map progress made and the 21st century challenges still ahead – from narrowing the digital divide to levelling the AI playing field – as the UN chief presented a “blueprint” to address promises that remain unfulfilled.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Millions of children return to schools that still can’t provide clean water or a working toilet
item.description: A new academic year is underway in many countries across the world, yet millions of children still attend schools where the water is unsafe to drink, toilets are unusable and there is nowhere to properly wash their hands.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: The grass beneath our feet: Why rangelands matter
item.description: In northern Kenya, a herder scans the sky for rain that hasn't come. The grass his animals need is thinning by the day.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global hunger declines again but progress remains uneven across regions
item.description: Global hunger declined for a third consecutive year in 2025 showing that progress is possible, but gains remain fragile and far too slow to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by the 2030 deadline.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As aid dries up, countries pledge to close the $4 trillion development gap
item.description: UN Member States reaffirmed their commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by adopting a declaration on Wednesday that they will implement reforms to help close the $4 trillion SDG financing gap.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Gaza aid challenges persist, renewed push for clean energy, Sudan cholera update
item.description: Humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to face significant challenges in reaching communities located near the so-called “Yellow Line” in northern Rafah, the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Despite hurdles, don’t give up on Sustainable Development Goals, UN urges
item.description: In a world of “parallel realities” where stark inequalities seemingly divide people and challenge the promise of multilateralism, the vision of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is to bring people together and help them achieve a better reality.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Thai youth leaders push for inclusion, partnership and lasting change
item.description: From local communities to the global stage, a diverse group of young leaders from Thailand is helping shape conversations on public policy, climate action, inclusion, indigenous rights, disability access and youth wellbeing.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Shared blueprint for peace’: Development goals deliver for billions, but challenges remain
item.description: With fewer than five years left to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a new UN report says sustained investment and international cooperation have improved billions of lives, but warns that governments must urgently accelerate action if the goals are to be met by their 2030 deadline.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: When AI hurts people, who’s to blame? Global experts grapple with accountability
item.description: Who is legally responsible when Artificial Intelligence causes harm? The issue took centre stage on Tuesday – day two of the first ever UN summit on AI governance, where leading experts warned of mounting evidence of human rights violations linked to the revolutionary technology.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Young people value partnership and parenthood but barriers block their dreams
item.description: Fertility rates are falling worldwide not because young people are rejecting marriage, children or family life but because many are facing economic and housing constraints.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Young peacebuilders: Funding matters, but so do trust and partnerships
item.description: Young people working on promoting peace in some of the world’s most fragile and polarised places say financial support remains essential, but money alone will not sustain their efforts to organize youth to participate in peacebuilding.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: How the stories we tell about ageing shape our future
item.description: The way societies talk about ageing can shape everything from public policy to people's own expectations of later life, the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) said on Wednesday in a new report that calls  for shifting away from narratives that portray older persons as a burden.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: New global rules clear the road for driverless vehicles
item.description: A UN vehicle standards forum has approved the first global regulations for fully autonomous driving systems (ADS), marking a major step towards the safe deployment of self-driving vehicles.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Khalida Popal and Javier Zanetti among football stars appointed UN Champions
item.description: With the World Cup just days away, 16 greats of the game have been appointed Football for the Goals (FFTG) Champions, using their profiles to raise awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and advocate for a better future for people and the planet.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global energy and trade disruption pushing millions towards poverty
item.description: Disruptions to global energy supplies and trade corridors are driving up the cost of food, transport and essential goods worldwide, slowing economic growth and increasing pressure on vulnerable households and debt-strapped developing countries.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN leads call to prepare ‘for when digital systems fail’
item.description: It can be annoying when the wifi signal is cut, but what about if everything digital we rely on were to crash suddenly – from satellites to life-support systems in hospitals?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Real impact on the ground’ needed as Indonesia backs UN reform
item.description: Indonesia is expecting a “strengthened multilateral system that delivers real impact on the ground,” as one of the key outcomes of the ongoing reform of the United Nations, that’s according to the country’s outgoing Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs for Multilateral Cooperation, Tri Tharyat.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI in advertising risks fuelling information crisis, UN warns
item.description: With spending on advertising topping $1 trillion a year worldwide, the United Nations on Wednesday highlighted the untapped power of major brands to shape the future of artificial intelligence (AI), warning that a failure to act could deepen a global information integrity crisis.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Tobago’s teen archery champion takes aim at sustainability targets
item.description: Six-time Trinidad and Tobago archery champion, Anthurium Lewis, has told UN News how sport helped her overcome age barriers in environmental advocacy and how in the future it can contribute to reaching globally agreed poverty and sustainability goals.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Youth shape the road to 2030, call for urgent action on sustainable development
item.description: As we confront increasingly complex and interconnected crises - from climate change to the AI revolution - the leadership and voices of young people have never been more vital, says the UN.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Why the ‘beautiful game’ is joining the fight for a better world
item.description: The world of football met the world of diplomacy this week as Brazilian World Cup legend Zico touched down at UN Headquarters in New York.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From misdiagnosis to medical bias: Why women are living longer but not better
item.description: For 25 years, the world has made significant progress in advancing women’s right to health, particularly in sexual and reproductive care. Women are living longer than ever before – but they are not living better.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Women leaders unite to advance gender equality, defend multilateralism amid growing global pushback
item.description: The Secretary-General’s commitment towards women leadership in the United Nations was recognized at a pivotal moment marked by global uncertainty, economic volatility and increasing pressure on hard-won rights.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nearly 5 million children are still dying annually before their fifth birthday: Here’s why
item.description: An estimated 4.9 million children died before their fifth birthday in 2024, including 2.3 million newborns, according to new United Nations estimates released on Tuesday – highlighting a worrying slowdown in global progress on child survival.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Over a billion fear losing land and homes within five years
item.description: Despite global progress in strengthening land tenure and governance, more than a billion people worldwide – nearly one in four adults – fear they could lose the rights to some or all of their land and housing within the next five years.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
